title: Airport sewer funding, longer debt terms, respect pledge
subtitle: Automated speed enforcement advocacy to the province, development charge pressures, and the Elect Respect pledge.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that the Region help pay for sewer and culvert work in Breslau, led by the Township of Woolwich, to serve the airport and nearby growth areas. Staff said the work would avoid a new pumping station previously budgeted at $15 million. The committee also recommended allowing debentures of up to 30 years for large growth-related projects with long useful lives {{vote:m3}}.

Councillors discussed a staff report on development charge reserves, which was received for information. They raised concerns about growing debt to pay for growth, the effect of provincial changes on when charges are collected, and asked for a broader long-term fiscal plan. Staff said this would be part of the 2026 budget process.

The committee recommended that the Region adopt the Elect Respect pledge on respectful civic participation {{vote:m4}}. It also recommended asking the province to standardize and add transparency to automated speed enforcement, after delegates raised concerns about signage and appeals {{vote:m5}}. Council still has to adopt these recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff enter agreements with Woolwich to fund up to $956,000 of a Randall Drain culvert and $510,000 toward design of a sanitary trunk and watermain, counted in lieu of airport development and connection charges {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended allowing staff to use debentures of up to 30 years for large growth-related projects with longer lives and future revenue cycles in future capital budgets.
The committee recommended that Council endorse the Elect Respect pledge, reject abuse and harassment, and forward the resolution to a list of governments, associations and police services.

The committee recommended asking the province to improve signage rules, require public reporting, standardize the program with municipalities, and direct ASE revenues to local road safety {{vote:m5}}.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them.

debate: Delegates on speed cameras said warning signs were obstructed, the appeal process relied on an online portal, and enforcement seemed aimed at revenue. One urged caution about technologies such as facial recognition. Staff said the process starts online but a person can be reached, and agreed to confirm this.

On the airport funding, a councillor asked what would be dropped from the capital plan to bring the work forward. Staff said reserves could cover it and later planned spending would be reviewed in the budget. Another asked whether Woolwich accepted counting the contributions in lieu of charges. Staff said more negotiation was needed and outside funding would likely be required.

On development charges, some councillors said growth-related debt and delayed collections are unsustainable and asked whether to favour infill over greenfield expansion. One asked for a whole-organization long-term fiscal plan. Staff said this would come through the 2026 budget.

On 30-year debentures, a councillor asked who decides which projects qualify. Staff said the criteria come from Municipal Act rules, including useful life, plus a legal review, and that the term would be added to the existing 10 and 20-year options.

On speed enforcement, the mover called the motion friendly advocacy for consistency across municipalities. One councillor opposed it, saying a provincial standard could be stricter than the Region's and that opposition to the cameras is growing.
